regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Ovarian, fallopian tube, peritoneal and selected other cancers
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: The NCCP lists high-risk early or advanced ovarian cancer, fallopian tube and primary peritoneal cancers, and selected advanced or recurrent endometrial, cervical or unknown-primary cancers. Ask which indication applies to you.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Ovarian, fallopian tube, peritoneal and selected other cancers
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Paclitaxel — It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected. Carboplatin — It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Both infusions every 21 days, for six planned cycles unless treatment ends earlier.
key_points: Paclitaxel runs first over about three hours, then carboplatin over about half an hour. Allow time for premedicines and checks.

NCCP Table 4: suggested paclitaxel dexamethasone 20 mg orally at approximately 12 and 6 hours, or IV 30 minutes before. Chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV 30 minutes before. Review the day-of-treatment dexamethasone with aprepitant (consider 12 mg). Reconcile the two steroid plans; individualise reductions or omissions with the consultant.
regimen_profiles.review_status: Feasibility build. Clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Relapsed ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This combination is used when one of these cancers returns after at least six months without recurrence following first-line platinum treatment.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Relapsed ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Gemcitabine — It interferes with copying DNA as cells divide. Blood-forming cells can also be affected. Carboplatin — It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Gemcitabine then carboplatin, both into a vein. Gemcitabine alone. The next cycle is planned three weeks after day 1 while treatment remains helpful and tolerable.
key_points: Each infusion usually takes about half an hour. Blood counts on day 8 can lead to a smaller gemcitabine dose or an omitted visit. An omitted dose is not made up in that cycle.
Day 1 includes carboplatin and requires the high-risk plan.
Day 8 is gemcitabine alone. Confirm the weekly blood tests and use the low-risk plan.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Ovarian, fallopian tube and primary peritoneal cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This schedule can be used after surgery for selected high-risk early ovarian cancers, or for advanced ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Ovarian, fallopian tube and primary peritoneal cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Paclitaxel — It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected. Carboplatin — It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Paclitaxel and carboplatin together. Paclitaxel alone on both visits. Repeat the cycle every 21 days. The planned course is 3–6 cycles after surgery or six in advanced disease, if suitable.
key_points: Paclitaxel runs over about an hour each week. Carboplatin follows it on day 1 only. You still attend on days 8 and 15.

NCCP Table 4: on day 1 the suggested paclitaxel premedicines are dexamethasone 8 mg IV, chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV 30 minutes before. Reconcile with antiemetic dexamethasone and local policy.

NCCP Table 4: from day 8 the suggested schedule is chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV 30 minutes before paclitaxel. Dexamethasone may be added for risk or prior reaction, and famotidine omission requires consultant guidance. Review the separate rechallenge pathway.
regimen_profiles.review_status: Feasibility build. Clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Platinum-sensitive relapsed ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This combination uses the pegylated liposomal formulation of doxorubicin with carboplatin for cancer that has returned and is considered sensitive to platinum.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Platinum-sensitive relapsed ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin — A fatty coating carries doxorubicin in the blood. The medicine damages DNA in dividing cells. Carboplatin — It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Both medicines every four weeks, usually for six cycles. Extra cycles may be considered if the cancer shrinks or stays stable.
key_points: Liposomal doxorubicin is given first, slowly at the start to watch for a reaction. Carboplatin follows. Report burning, swelling or pain around your drip immediately.
Use the pegylated liposomal formulation. Prior anthracycline exposure, cardiac function, infusion reactions, stomatitis and hand–foot toxicity require review.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Previously treated dMMR or MSI-high endometrial cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This immunotherapy is for advanced or recurrent womb cancer that progressed during or after platinum treatment and has a tumour test showing mismatch repair deficiency or high microsatellite instability.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Previously treated dMMR or MSI-high endometrial cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Dostarlimab — It removes a brake on immune cells so they can recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause inflammation in healthy organs.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: One infusion every three weeks for four doses. Dose 5 is three weeks after dose 4. After dose 5 the interval is six weeks, while treatment remains suitable.
key_points: Dostarlimab goes into a vein over about 30 minutes. Only dostarlimab is used on this pathway. Keep the immunotherapy alert card with you after treatment too.
Minimal emetic risk. Check the immunotherapy alert card. Evaluate diarrhoea, vomiting and endocrine symptoms for immune toxicity before routine symptomatic treatment.

evidence_records.evidence_context: Ovarian, fallopian tube, peritoneal and selected other cancers
key_findings: In patients with optimally resected stage III ovarian cancer, the carboplatin combination was easier to tolerate and achieved comparable cancer control to cisplatin with paclitaxel.
evidence_records.limitations: The trial population was specific to ovarian cancer. Other indications have their own evidence and treatment goals.

evidence_records.evidence_context: Relapsed ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer
key_findings: In a randomised trial in platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer, median time before progression was 8.6 months with the combination and 5.8 months with carboplatin alone.
evidence_records.limitations: The trial did not establish an overall survival advantage. Group medians cannot predict an individual outcome.

evidence_records.evidence_context: Ovarian, fallopian tube and primary peritoneal cancer
key_findings: In the US randomised study, weekly paclitaxel did not significantly prolong time before cancer progression in the overall study population compared with three-weekly paclitaxel.
evidence_records.limitations: Bevacizumab use varied. This result does not predict which schedule will suit an individual.

evidence_records.evidence_context: Platinum-sensitive relapsed ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer
key_findings: In platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer, median time to progression was 11.3 months with this combination versus 9.4 months with carboplatin and paclitaxel. The combinations had different side effects.
evidence_records.limitations: This comparison concerned recurrent disease. A median describes the trial group.

evidence_records.evidence_context: Previously treated dMMR or MSI-high endometrial cancer
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Objective response rate and duration of response
key_findings: In the GARNET trial, measurable tumour shrinkage was seen in about 46 in 100 evaluable people in the mismatch repair deficient or MSI-high endometrial cancer group.
evidence_records.limitations: This was a single-arm trial. A response rate does not tell us how long someone will live or how the medicine compares directly with another treatment.
